headline: On November 20, 1980: Lake Peigneur drains into a salt mine
captionCards: The collapse created a 150-foot-wide sinkhole and altered the local geography
instagramCaption:
Lake Peigneur vanished in minutes.

A drilling error by Texaco pierced the Diamond Crystal Salt Mine beneath the lake. Water rushed down, eroding the mine’s edges and collapsing the lake floor. The lake, 200 feet deep, drained into the underground salt deposit. A 150-foot-wide sinkhole formed, swallowing boats and trees.

The event reshaped Louisiana’s landscape and became a case study in geological risk. 

What would you have done if your backyard suddenly disappeared?
